Who this worksheet is for

This Year 9 / KS3 worksheet focuses on quadratic expressions with coefficient 1 on x². Learners find integer pairs using the product and sum, then work with negative signs, repeated factors and the difference of two squares.

The main PDF has four lesson and exercise pages followed by two solution pages. A separate two-page Expanding and Factorising homework provides mixed follow-up practice and worked answers. This is the same companion homework included with Expanding Double Brackets, so there is no need to download it twice.

6 pages + 2-page homework · Answers

What the worksheet covers

  • Finding integer pairs with the required product and sum
  • Choosing positive and negative bracket signs
  • Repeated factors and squared brackets
  • Difference of two squares
  • Using area factors to find rectangle sides and perimeter
  • Checking claims, independent practice and mixed homework

Prerequisites: expanding double brackets and working confidently with negative numbers. The lesson treats quadratics with x² coefficient 1 and integer factor pairs, not all quadratic expressions. Use separate paper for working. Homework timing is a flexible aim; teaching marks are suggestions rather than an official exam-board scheme.

Key ideas at a glance

Match both the product and the sum

For x² + bx + c = (x + p)(x + q), the numbers must satisfy pq = c and p + q = b. This method needs a suitable integer pair when factorising into integer brackets.

Check the signs by expanding

For x² - 2x - 15, the pair is 3 and -5, giving (x + 3)(x - 5). Reversing the two signs would produce the wrong middle term.
